Halo 3 was one of the first FPS games my father introduced me to when I was a kid. I spent hours on the Xbox playing Halo 3's campaign and replaying it as Master Chief really did inspire me. Those days were some of the best, and while I sometimes wish I could go back, growing up is part of life. For this reason, I purchase the Master Chief Collection to relive part of my childhood and show my deepest gratitude to Halo for being an integral of my childhood. I also wanted to get a better understanding of the story, especially since I never got the chance to play Halo Reach, Halo 2, and Halo: CE. With that said, I don't regret my purchase and highly recommend others to give Halo a try.

While I have been a fan of the Halo series as long as I can remember, I am severely disappointed in the Halo MCC pc launch. There have been many unexplainable issues with every update (and yes, I get porting games to PC can be very difficult but what happened to launching "when it's ready"). Every game I play I get East US servers with horrible hit reg, and on top of that I have yet to play a match with my brothers and cousin in the same game because of connection interrupted issues that have been happening since MCC came to PC. I was so excited to play this but there are just too many issues that aren't being addressed/fixed and it makes the game unplayable.

This game has received multiple updates and is better than launch but there are still problems rooted in the game.

Highly recommended.

The ultimate collection for the Halo saga.
• Includes the iconic original trilogy—an absolute must-have
• Features some great enhancements
• Keeps one of the most enjoyable multiplayer experiences alive
• Boasts one of the greatest and most immersive soundtracks of all time

Even though I’ve played these games on different platforms and originally completed them all on Game Pass, this collection is essential for anyone who loves shooters and epic stories.

Experience the complete journey of all halo games remastered, with never before added in game lore. By viewing terminals scattered throughout maps, players can uncover the backstory behind past civilizations like the forerunners. There's a feature that lets players switch between the classic and remastered versions on the fly, even in cutscenes. You can't deny the effort and dedication the devs have spent in remastering these titles, breathing new life to multiplayer no less. Simply a must buy and worth every penny.

This offers great value, even when the game is not on sale. This contains all of the Master Chief campaigns, multiplayer for those games (including Spartan Ops), with ODST and Reach serving as separate DLC that needs to be bought (once it is, then I believe Firefight will become available).. This is a classic shooter that offers a fun narrative. While I have mostly played this game in co-op, I am doing a solo run on Heroic (for the most part). The checkpoint system is really great, too; in all of my years playing, the worst checkpoint I got was when I accidentally fell off a cliff on a Chopper in Halo.

I cannot recommend this game enough.

This is a fun collection of games, I remember playing CE back in the day as a wee tot. If you like blasting aliens and finishing the fight, this is the collection for you. Start in Reach, end in 4 if you want the chronological playthrough. ODST happens during Halo 2.

The multiplayer is where memories are made, but I haven't been there in ages except with a select group of friends. You have Forge where you can edit and make your own custom maps and gamemodes, you have Firefight where you fight hordes of aliens. And as always, the Campaign. All I can say is find what you want to do and do it.

tldr.text: Very Positive (92%): players praise the co-op most of all.
12% of reviews complain about bugs and crashes, the most common complaint.

details.text: Bugs and crashes are far less common lately, with 5% of recent reviews complaining, against 12% all time.

Buyers should know recent reviews mention accounts and launchers slightly more often, with one saying "cannot recommend the Steam version to anyone who wants to play the campaigns without a Microsoft account".
